messages:
elaine: Heads up — noticing intermittent TX drops and interface flaps on a subset of c7gn GPU nodes in eu-west-1.
raj: Which NIC/driver? any pattern by AZ or instance SKU?
elaine: mlx5_core + Mellanox firmware on these hosts (SKU: c7gn.48xlarge). Seems concentrated on a handful of racks in az-2.
elaine: Quick paste from one host: 
```
$ ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'tx_err|tx_drops'
ethtool: stats for eth0
tx_errors: 0
tx_dropped: 4321
tx_retries: 0
```
raj: TX_dropped nonzero but tx_errors 0. dmesg shows firmware resets?
elaine: yup — got repeated logs: "mlx5_core 0000:66:00.0: firmware failed: status -5, resetting device"
swe-oncall: Are we seeing packet loss on east-west traffic or only host-internal? any perf regression for inference jobs?
maria: Customer-facing jobs in that AZ saw tail latency spikes ~200ms for small batch chat workloads, correlated with node requeues.
raj: Can we reproduce with iperf3 or netperf between two affected nodes? also check MTU/jumbo frames mismatch.
elaine: Ran quick iperf3 between two nodes in same rack: showed periodic drops and retransmits. MTU was 9001 on both.
elaine: Also tried disabling jumbo (mtu 1500) on a test node — drops stopped after switch but still seeing occasional firmware resets.
infra-bot: Incident ticket created: INF-2026-947 — network firmware errors impacting EU-WEST-1 az-2, priority P2.
vendor-net: Thanks for flagging — can you capture mlx5 firmware versions (ethtool -i) and logs? We have a suspected regression in FW 21.32.
elaine: `ethtool -i eth0` -> driver: mlx5_core, version: 5.18.21, firmware-version: 22.10.0
raj: That firmware-version doesn't match vendor-suspected 21.32; might be newer but buggy. Any nodes with older firmware that are stable?
maria: We have a handful in same cluster on firmware 20.14 and they look fine.
raj: Plan: (1) cordon & drain one affected rack for a canary firmware rollback, (2) run stress tests and netperf, (3) if stable, schedule rolling rollback for az-2. Need approval for capacity impact.
swe-oncall: Can we shift ML workloads to other AZs temporarily? Capacity is tight but we have ~30% spare in az-1.
elaine: I'll start draining two nodes now (canary). tagging them with `nic-fw-canary`.
elaine: Command used: `kubectl drain gpu-node-az2-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
raj: Also capture tcpdump around a flap to attach to vendor ticket: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/eth0-flap.pcap` — keep short due to disk.
elaine: Captured pcap and dmesg. Uploaded to ticket INF-2026-947.
vendor-net: We reviewed the logs; lets coordinate a rollback to firmware 20.14 on the canary nodes. We'll provide an automated script. ETA 45m.
maria: Heads up to SRE — we need runbook for rollback + rollback-back plan. Also communicate to oncall rotation.
raj: Runbook snippet: 1) cordon -> 2) drain -> 3) apply fw-rollback script -> 4) reboot NIC -> 5) run netperf -> 6) uncordon. If failure, reprovision from spare pool and revert.
elaine: After rollback on canary nodes we saw no new firmware resets for 2 hours and netperf stable (no retransmits).
infra-bot: Update INF-2026-947: canary rollback showed success. Scheduling rolling rollback window tomorrow 02:00-06:00 UTC for az-2.
swe-oncall: Add mitigation: autoscale down ML batch queues during window and route critical latency-sensitive traffic to az-1.
raj: Post-rollout tasks: run full cluster RDMA sanity, validate KV cache and inter-node KV replication for serving runtime.
maria: Noted — I'll update status page and ping partners. Also check billing/cost impact from cross-AZ traffic during mitigation.
elaine: Thanks team — I'll keep monitoring and post follow-ups in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
